label: end-of-episode clock (last ~10 trials), strongest at GO and on a2 trials
explanation: An episode-end timer unit. It never fires before episode trial 80: 97% of activation mass is in trials 90-99, and it fires only when the value head is low (value < 5.22 covers 99.97% of mass, recall 0.997). Within that window it ramps up toward the episode end, and 82% of mass is at GO, where it is strongest when the upcoming choice is a2 (GO & a2 & trial>=90 has precision 0.83). It is weaker on a2 / S2 D2 steps and on unrewarded D1 steps, and it never fires on a rewarded D1 input (in_rew==1). It is mostly silent on a1 / S1 inputs. The recorded predicate (trial>=92, not a rewarded-D1 step, GO or an a2 trial) uses action, which is the agent own upcoming choice at D1 (a legitimate computed variable); at D2 it is observed. The fully observed alternative (ep_trial>=90) & (in_rew != 1) & (in_action != 1) & (in_state != 1) gets dev F1 0.61 with mass recall 0.96. Precision stays near 0.55 because the unit grows gradually over the final trials, so the onset is soft and a binary predicate cannot capture it. Magnitude is driven by closeness to the episode end and the GO phase. This is not a reward or transition feature: rates are flat across core patterns and transitions.
